findings.claim: Every request body is exactly [system=SYSTEM_PROMPT, user=USER_TEMPLATE filled]. Each byte-equals the reconstruction from the recorded model_view, history_shown and remaining_shown. No request reached the server without a receipt.
findings.evidence: For all 64 call rows, req017_adapter.build_messages plus canonical_body(alias, settings) equals the receipt body under json equality and json.dumps(sort_keys, ensure_ascii=False) text equality. body_sha256 matches in 64/64. There are exactly 2 messages, and the only body keys are model, messages, temperature=0, max_tokens=1536 and stream=false. The server log has 64 slot launches. Its completion-token and prompt_n sequences match the 64 outcome receipts in order. Each recorded reply equals choices[0].message.content, and finish_reason and usage match. remaining_shown = 16-(n-1). history_shown follows exactly from prior parsed actions and error_excerpt(action_error). For executed steps, the next row's model_view.last_action_error equals that step's action_error, and model_view is unchanged after invalid replies. The prompt sha 119a3984... and the sha256 of all 6 adapter and runner files match the frozen manifest.

findings.claim: No model input contains a forbidden marker or a verifier field.
findings.evidence: The 13 case-sensitive FORBIDDEN_MARKERS return 0 hits in the full body JSON and message text. Case-insensitive scans for file:, data-price, data-duration, wob_, raw_reward and done return 0 hits. So do DONE_GLOBAL, RAW_REWARD_GLOBAL, REWARD_GLOBAL, REWARD_REASON, EPISODE_ID, TASK_READY, task_info, verifier, browsergym_reward, terminated, truncated, info_error, dom_object, url, http, screenshot, last_action_error, 'call log', 'data-', localhost, .html and href. The only generic hit is 'result' in 51 bodies, from the page's visible autocomplete live-region text ('1 result is available...'), which is not a verifier field. Every model_view has exactly the keys goal, axtree and last_action_error. last_action_error is never interpolated; it reaches the model only as the history excerpt. No leak_guard rows were written, and no fill value contains a marker, so the typed-exemption path was never used.

findings.claim: History error excerpts are first-line only and markup-free. The markup-bearing Playwright call logs were never shown.
findings.evidence: All 24 raw action_errors have several lines, and in every one the lines after the first contain '<' markup. None contains data-price, data-duration, data-result, file:, WOB_, miniwob or book-flight.html. The shown excerpts are 'TimeoutError: Locator.fill: Timeout 500ms exceeded.' (23) and 'TimeoutError: Locator.click: Timeout 500ms exceeded.' (1). No history line in any user message contains '<'. Every '>' in the bodies is part of a history arrow ('-> ok' / '-> error:'): 326 arrows and 0 other '>'.

findings.claim: Every executed action is a canonical click/fill/noop whose bid was a line-leading [bid] of that step's model_view tree. Re-running parse_action reproduces every recorded parse, and REQ-017 differs from REQ-016 only on the 6 canonicalized rows.
findings.evidence: 46 executed actions: 14 click, 30 fill and 2 noop. All match repr form click('<bid>') / fill('<bid>', '<text>') / noop(). No executed bid contains a bracket, and each appears in tree_bids and as ^\t*[bid] in that step's tree. req017_adapter.parse_action(reply, model_view.axtree) returns (parsed_action, invalid_cause, invalid_detail) identical to the recording in 64/64 rows. req016_adapter.parse_action gives the same result on every row except the 6 canonicalized ones, where it returns unknown_bid. The canonicalized replies are 300/1 fill('[19]'), 300/4 fill('[25]'), 301/10 fill('[19]') followed by an explanatory line beginning '[19] is...', 302/1 fill('[19]'), 302/9 click('[27]') and 303/1 fill('[19]'). All 6 have invalid_cause null and invalid_detail equal to the canonicalization note, and all were executed. None of the 18 invalid rows was executed, and none has action_error, verifier_only or screenshot fields.

findings.claim: Interface observation, not an exposure violation: most rejections trace back to the prompt/history format. 8 of 9 no_action replies echo the history arrow format, and all 9 multiple_actions replies (seed 301) used bracketed ids that the bracket rule does not rescue in multi-line replies.
findings.evidence: 8 of 9 no_action replies contain '->' and 5 end in '-> ok' (e.g. 300/2 "fill('21', 'Carlsbad, CA') -> ok"; 301/14-16). All 9 seed-301 multiple_actions replies contain '[id]' calls, e.g. "fill('[19]', 'Wales, AK')\n\nclick('[27]')". Rejecting them is correct under the frozen grammar, so it does not affect exposure validity. It is relevant to the lead's interpretation of the 0/4 result.

findings.claim: 23 of the 24 action errors are fill() calls on the readonly datepicker input [25]; the other is a click on status [30]. The model was never shown why fill failed: its error excerpt is the first line only and the tree shows no readonly marker.
findings.evidence: All 23 fill errors read 'TimeoutError: Locator.fill: Timeout 500ms exceeded.', and their call logs show '<input readonly ... id="datepicker">' and 'element is not editable'. findings.claim: Seed 302 (cheapest, ISN to MPB, 10/02/2016) typed From and To, then looped on fill [25] (10 errors) and clicked Search 3 times with the date empty. The datepicker was never opened.

findings.claim: The id format changed once an executed action appeared in history. Up to and including the first executed action, all 24 click/fill action lines used brackets; afterwards only 2 of 40 did. A new failure mode also appeared: 9 no_action replies, 8 of which copy the history's '-> ...' suffix. REQ-016 had no no_action replies.
findings.evidence: The history_lines() format is 'N. <action> -> ok' / '-> error: ...', which REQ-016 never displayed because nothing executed there. In REQ-017, 5 invalid replies end in '-> ok' (300 s02, 301 s14-s16, 303 s03) and 3 more contain '->' (301 s12, s13, 302 s03). Bracketed ids after the first execution: 300 s04 '[25]' and 302 s09 '[27]'. Overall, strict click/fill action lines were 26 bracketed and 38 bare. Across all 78 call substrings: 26 bracketed, 48 bare, 2 '<id>' placeholders, 2 noop. This is an association in 4 episodes, not a tested cause.

findings.claim: The line-based one-action rule executed 5 replies that contain a second call-like expression inside a non-action line. Only the fill was executed.
findings.evidence: 302 s08 and 303 s07-s10 contain "[25] textbox '' -> click('25')" (or click('<id>')) on one line, followed by a separate fill('25', ...) line. _candidate() only counts lines that are exactly one call, so these parse as a single fill; the embedded click was not executed. This follows the inherited REQ-016 rule and is not an adapter defect, but the '9 multi-action replies' figure counts only strict lines (the any-substring count is 14).

findings.claim: Compared with REQ-016 (same model, GGUF, system prompt, T=0, max_tokens 1536; different seeds 200-207; the only change is the adapter), the model's first move is the same but the outcome differs: REQ-016 executed 0 of 128 calls, while REQ-017 executed 46 of 64.
findings.evidence: The REQ-016 and REQ-017 receipts share one system prompt, and every seed in both runs opens with fill('[19]', ...). In REQ-016, 263 of 263 strict action lines were bracketed; there were 62 unknown_bid and 66 multiple_actions (51.6%) replies, with multi-action in all 8 seeds. All 62 unknown_bid replies re-parse as valid under the REQ-017 parser when checked statically against their stored trees. Conversely, the REQ-016 parser would statically reject 6 of the 64 REQ-017 replies, the canonicalized ones. Because trajectories are path-dependent, this static re-parse is not a counterfactual rollout. REQ-017 has multi-action in 9/64 replies (14.1%), all in seed 301. Tokens: REQ-016 used 45,832 prompt and 3,694 completion (358 prompt/call); REQ-017 used 37,744 and 1,777 (590 prompt/call). 9,499 REQ-017 prompt tokens came from 6 calls whose tree included the calendar (~1,438-1,675 each).

findings.claim: The publisher sanitizes only .json/.jsonl/.md/.txt/.log files, so child_config.json.guarded is published byte-for-byte without sanitization. It is clean here only because its bytes were copied from an already-sanitized file.
findings.evidence: In req016_screen.publish, the suffix whitelist is ('.json', '.jsonl', '.md', '.txt', '.log'). req017_episodes.main writes child_config.json.guarded as a raw byte copy of child_config.json, which write_json_x had already sanitized (out_dir './work/runs/...'). findings.claim: The REQ-017 admission conflict fields carry inherited REQ-016 names even though they check REQ-017 state.

findings.claim: The publication is complete and hash-exact, and the scan found no username or secret-like strings.
findings.evidence: There are 199 raw files, 199 publication_manifest entries and 200 published files (the extra one is publication_manifest.json). Every raw_sha256 and published_sha256 recomputes, and the sanitized flags are exact: only server_small_...log.txt (absolute model path replaced by '.') and watchdog_config.json.
